Classes suspended in Sultan Kudarat amid extreme heat
COTABATO CITY, Philippines — Sultan Kudarat Governor Pax Ali Mangudadatu ordered the suspension of classes at all levels in public and private schools across the province starting Monday, November 23, due to dangerously high temperatures forecast by the state weather bureau.
In an order issued Sunday, Mangudadatu said the suspension was intended to protect students, teachers and school personnel from possible heat-related illnesses.
“This is a precaution against elevated heat index levels and possible heat-related illnesses,” the governor said.
The suspension also covers on-campus examinations, physical education classes and outdoor school activities.
According to the Philippine Atmospheric, Geophysical and Astronomical Services Administration (PAGASA), the heat index in Sultan Kudarat and other parts of the Soccsksargen Region is expected to reach 37 to 38 degrees Celsius on Monday and Tuesday.
Classes are expected to resume Tuesday, November 24, unless the provincial government issues another directive.
Mangudadatu urged residents to take precautions against the intense heat, particularly by drinking enough water and avoiding prolonged exposure to high temperatures.

At least two areas in Palawan are forecast to record “danger” level heat index on Monday, November 23, 2026, according to state weather bureau PAGASA.
In its forecast issued Sunday, PAGASA said the following weather stations are expected to record heat index readings ranging from 42°C to 51°C, classified as “danger” level:
Coron, Palawan – 42°C
Cuyo, Palawan – 43°C
PAGASA warned that prolonged exposure to danger-level heat may cause heat cramps and heat exhaustion, while heat stroke is “probable with continued exposure.”
On Sunday, November 22, Cuyo had already recorded a danger-level heat index of 42°C.
Heat index refers to the temperature felt by the human body when relative humidity is combined with actual air temperature. High humidity slows the evaporation of sweat, making it harder for the body to cool down.
PAGASA advised the public to limit outdoor activities and use protective gear, such as hats or umbrellas, when going outside.
The agency also reminded the public to stay hydrated by drinking plenty of water and avoiding tea, coffee, alcohol and carbonated beverages.— MCG, GMA News

Brace yourselves for snow, traffic chaos and gale-force winds at sea.
An orange weather warning for heavy snowfall and strong winds along the E4 motorway from north of Uppsala to just south of Gävle remains in place until noon on Monday, following a spate of crashes across Sweden on Sunday.
The weather risks creating very difficult driving conditions, according to Sweden's national weather agency, SMHI.
There's also a yellow warning for snow and wind in place for eastern Svealand until Monday afternoon, which could also cause traffic disruption – plus, a yellow warning for snowfall in the southernmost coastal areas of Gävleborg as well as parts of the Uppsala region, which remains active until Tuesday evening and could bring 10-20 centimetres of snow.
None of the traffic accidents on Sunday resulted in serious injuries. Several vehicles skidded off the E4 between Nyköping and Tystberga, with drivers reporting icy conditions along the stretch, according to public radio broadcaster Sveriges Radio.

At sea, yellow warnings for gale-force winds are in place along most of Sweden's east coast.
Ferry operator Destination Gotland cancelled or delayed several sailings between Gotland and the mainland.
